report:
## Conclusion

The claim is well supported: the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) substantially reduces herpes zoster (shingles) in adults aged 70 and older.

## Evidence

The pivotal randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind ZOE-70 trial (NCT01165229) enrolled ~14,000 adults aged 70+ across 18 countries, randomizing them to two doses of RZV or placebo. The trial found high vaccine efficacy against shingles specifically in this age group, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine (Lopman et al., "Efficacy of the Herpes Zoster Subunit Vaccine in Adults 70 Years of Age or Older," NEJM 2016) (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800). This built on the companion ZOE-50 trial in adults 50+, which showed 97.2% efficacy overall (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184).

Long-term follow-up (ZOSTER-049 extension study) of ZOE-50/70 participants demonstrated durable protection, with efficacy remaining high roughly 10 years after vaccination, and end-of-trial data showing 79.7% efficacy in participants 50+ over 6–11 years, with efficacy at 82.0% at year 11 (https://academic.oup.com/ofid/article/9/10/ofac485/6766954).

Beyond clinical trials, real-world evidence corroborates these findings: a 2025 target trial emulation study using Medicare claims data, published in Annals of Internal Medicine and summarized by UNC researchers, confirmed RZV effectively prevents shingles in adults 65+, including immunocompromised individuals, with two doses offering superior protection over one (https://www.med.unc.edu/fammed/2025/10/21/unc-study-confirms-shingles-vaccine-effectiveness-in-older-adults/).

The CDC also states that in adults 70+ with healthy immune systems, vaccine-induced immunity remains high for at least 7 years (https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/vaccines/index.html).

## Bottom line

Multiple lines of evidence—randomized controlled trial data specific to the 70+ age group, long-term follow-up studies, and real-world observational data—consistently confirm that RZV substantially reduces shingles risk in adults aged 70 and older.
